content.text: The analysis is clear. The zone's own cooling setpoint stayed constant (≈25.1–25.3 °C) across 2018, and its neighboring zones (F3_Z02, F3_Z03, F3_Z05) did NOT rise — in fact they drift slightly down — while the F3_Z01 sensor reading steadily climbs from ~24.4 °C (Jun–Jul) to ~25.1 °C (Oct–Dec), i.e. it moves up toward its own (unchanged) cooling setpoint and away from the unchanged setpoint. A single-zone, monotonic drift consistent with rising cooling demand, with a stable setpoint, is a local load change, not a sensor fault (a sensor fault would typically produce erratic readings, saturation, or divergence from the setpoint, and not a smooth rise while peer zones stay stable).
